questions: Did progress rise above 0.155 on the s-bend and above 0.107 on the slalom, compared with iteration 5?
Did max_error stay at or below 0.069 on every track? If it rose, at what progress does the robot leave the track?
Did steering_oscillation rise with the higher ground speed, and is the controller gain now too high for it?
Did any run finish, and if so, what is the completion_time?

intent: Revert wheel_track to 0.12 m, the value that held progress in iteration 5 (both narrowing in iteration 3 and widening in iteration 7 lowered progress). Keep mass 0.6 kg and the iteration 5 sensor layout and footprint. Raise wheel_radius from 0.035 m to 0.04 m to test whether a further speed step raises progress on the s-bend and slalom. Expected result: s-bend progress above 0.155, slalom progress above 0.107, and max_error at or below 0.069 on all tracks.
learning: Iterations 3 and 7 show that the track is tuned near 0.12 m, so further track changes are unlikely to help. Iteration 6 shows that lower mass hurts at this speed. Speed is the remaining geometry lever. If wheel_radius 0.04 m raises progress with max_error held, speed still helps and I will consider a further step. If progress is flat or max_error exceeds 0.069, I will stop changing geometry and ask the Integrator to raise kp or kd at this speed.
rationale: Iteration 7 (wheel_track 0.14 m, with iteration 5's other values) scored 48.83, below the iteration 5 best of 51.01. Progress fell on the s-bend (0.155 to 0.145) and the slalom (0.107 to 0.100), and max_error on the s-bend rose slightly (0.065 to 0.0647, about flat). Iteration 3 also lowered s-bend progress, but by narrowing the track to 0.10 m. Progress therefore dropped in both directions away from 0.12 m, so 0.12 m is the track the robot is currently tuned to, and turn rate is not what limits it. Iteration 6 showed that lowering mass to 0.5 kg also lowers progress and raises max_error, so mass stays at 0.6 kg. Speed is the only lever that has raised progress without pushing max_error past the 0.069 band (iteration 5: wheel_radius 0.03 to 0.035 m gave s-bend progress 0.149 to 0.155). I therefore revert wheel_track to 0.12 m, keep mass 0.6 kg and the iteration 5 sensor layout (sensor_size 0.012 m, x = -0.03 to 0.03 m, y = 0.04 m), and take the next speed step, wheel_radius 0.035 to 0.04 m. The expected result is progress above 0.155 on the s-bend and above 0.107 on the slalom, with max_error at or below 0.069. If progress does not rise, or max_error goes above 0.069, speed has reached its useful limit and the next step is a controller change for the Integrator rather than more geometry.
